subsystems.name: Physical qubits
subsystems.role: the noisy hardware that stores the encoded information.
parts: data qubits (superconducting transmons, trapped ions or neutral atoms)

subsystems.name: Encoding lattice
subsystems.role: arranges data and ancilla qubits into the two-dimensional pattern the chosen code requires.
parts: boundary qubits that define the logical operators

subsystems.name: Syndrome extraction
subsystems.role: repeatedly measures stabiliser operators without collapsing the encoded state.

subsystems.name: Real-time decoder
subsystems.role: turns the stream of measured syndromes into a correction fast enough to keep up.
parts: low-latency link to the control system

subsystems.name: Control and cryogenics
subsystems.role: keeps the qubits cold and delivers precise pulses at scale.

subsystems.name: Logical gate layer
subsystems.role: operates on logical qubits while limiting how errors spread.

buildSteps.title: Choose the code and error model
buildSteps.detail: Pick a stabiliser code such as the surface code and set its distance from the measured single- and two-qubit gate errors and measurement errors of the hardware.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate and wire the physical qubits
buildSteps.detail: Make data and ancilla qubits and couple them only to their neighbours; for superconducting circuits this means patterned aluminium or niobium films on a silicon chip, for neutral atoms it means loading atoms into optical tweezers and rearranging them.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate every operation
buildSteps.detail: Tune single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, measurement and reset, then benchmark them with randomised benchmarking until the error per operation is below the code's threshold — roughly one percent for the surface code.

buildSteps.title: Initialise the logical qubit
buildSteps.detail: Prepare a known logical state by measuring all stabilisers and projecting into the code space, then verify it with logical state tomography.

buildSteps.title: Run repeated syndrome cycles
buildSteps.detail: Each cycle entangles each ancilla with its neighbouring data qubits, measures the ancilla and resets it, producing a fresh set of parity outcomes.

buildSteps.title: Decode in real time
buildSteps.detail: Feed syndromes to an FPGA running a matching or neural-network decoder; it maintains a history of probable errors and outputs a correction before the next cycle of errors accumulates.

buildSteps.title: Apply corrections and track the Pauli frame
buildSteps.detail: Low-level corrections are often tracked in software rather than applied physically, while the final measurement outcomes are reinterpreted at the end of the computation.

buildSteps.title: Scale to logical gates and more qubits
buildSteps.detail: Encode many logical qubits, entangle them with lattice surgery, and add magic-state distillation to obtain the non-Clifford gates needed for universal computation.

prerequisites.tech: Physical qubits below the fault-tolerance threshold
prerequisites.why: if gates and measurements are too noisy, adding more qubits makes the logical error worse rather than better; below-threshold behaviour has been shown only in small codes.
ancillas must be measured and reset repeatedly during a computation without disturbing the data qubits.
the decoder must finish before the next syndrome cycle; this is microseconds for superconducting qubits and is hard to sustain on large lattices.

prerequisites.tech: Scalable control wiring and cryogenic electronics
prerequisites.why: thousands of qubits need thousands of control lines, and routing them without adding heat or noise is unsolved at scale.

prerequisites.tech: Fabrication and tuning yield at scale
prerequisites.why: a single useful logical qubit may need thousands of physical qubits, all working and calibrated simultaneously.

pathway.milestone: small logical qubits with demonstrated error suppression — a 2023 surface-code experiment and 2023 atom-array logical processors
pathway.unlocks: proof that encoding and repeated syndrome extraction can reduce logical error rate.

pathway.milestone: logical error falling exponentially as code distance grows, sustained over many cycles
pathway.unlocks: a genuine fault-tolerance threshold, the point where scaling qubits actually helps.

pathway.milestone: hundreds of logical qubits with logical entangling gates and distillation
pathway.unlocks: fault-tolerant machines able to run deep quantum circuits.
chemistry, materials and cryptanalysis problems beyond classical reach.
